title.rendered: Cost of Prefab Homes in India

content.rendered:
The cost of prefab homes in India is not one number — it is a range that moves with size, configuration, materials, finish and transport. A small factory-built cabin home starts in the low lakhs; a multi-room prefabricated house runs higher. This guide explains what actually drives the price, with real starting figures from SAMAN's own range, so you can budget before you enquire.

SAMAN POS India Private Limited (POS = Portable Office Solutions) manufactures steel-framed prefab homes to order and prices each one to your plan — the figures below are real starting points, not a flat rate.

What Drives the Cost of a Prefab Home

  • Size and room count: the single biggest driver. A one-room cabin home costs a fraction of a multi-room house.
  • Configuration: single-level vs G+1, number of bathrooms, kitchen fit-out and partitions.
  • Materials and insulation: an IS 2062 MS steel frame with insulated PUF panels costs more than bare sheeting, but controls heat and lasts longer.
  • Finish level: flooring, cladding, electricals and fittings move the figure up or down.
  • Transport: delivery distance from the factory to your site affects the landed cost.

Because these vary, a prefab home is quoted against your actual plan rather than a fixed per-square-foot rate.

Real Starting Prices From SAMAN

From our live prefabricated houses range:

  • Portable cabin house — an entry living cabin from ₹2,56,000.
  • Porta cabin house — a compact factory-built home from ₹3,65,000.
  • Multi-room prefabricated house — larger configured homes from ₹16,25,000, built to your room plan.

These are genuine starting points for real configurations; your final figure depends on the size and finish you choose.

Prefab Cost vs Conventional Construction

A prefab home is usually cheaper to own over its life than an equivalent RCC build, for reasons beyond the headline price: it is built far faster (so you occupy or earn from it sooner), the cost is fixed at a known specification rather than open-ended site work, and a steel-framed unit can be relocated rather than written off. Delivery is ₹3,000 default with a 3–5 day transit on standard units.

FAQs: Cost of Prefab Homes

What is the cheapest prefab home from SAMAN?
An entry portable cabin house starts from ₹2,56,000; a compact porta cabin house from ₹3,65,000. Larger multi-room houses start from ₹16,25,000.

Is prefab cheaper than conventional construction?
Usually, over the life of the building — it builds faster, the cost is fixed to a specification, and the steel unit can be relocated. The exact saving depends on your design.

Does the price include delivery?
Standard units carry ₹3,000 default delivery with 3–5 day transit; longer distances are quoted to your location.

How to Read a Prefab Home Quote

When you compare prefab home quotes, read them by their parts rather than the headline number:

  • Structure: is the frame IS 2062 structural steel, sized to your load and wind zone, or a lighter under-specified section?
  • Insulation: are the walls and roof insulated PUF panels, or bare sheeting that heats up?
  • What is factory-fitted: wiring, plumbing points and finish done before dispatch versus left for site work.
  • Delivery and assembly: whether transport to your location and on-site assembly are included.

A low quote that leaves out insulation, fittings or delivery is rarely the cheaper home once you complete it. SAMAN prices each home to your plan and makes every line explicit, so you can compare like for like.

Who Buys Prefab Homes in India

Prefab homes suit plot owners building a weekend or retirement home, businesses needing fast staff accommodation, farm owners wanting a durable field house, and developers after a repeatable housing format. In every case the appeal is a finished, durable, relocatable steel home built to a fixed cost and timeline rather than an open-ended site project.

Total Cost of Ownership, Not Just the Sticker Price

The headline price is only part of the picture. A prefab home reaches usable condition far faster than an RCC build, so you start living in it — or earning rent from it — sooner. The IS 2062 steel frame with insulated panels needs little maintenance compared with masonry, and because the unit is relocatable it retains value as a movable asset rather than being tied to one plot. When you weigh build time, maintenance and flexibility alongside the purchase price, a factory-built home is usually the lower lifetime cost for the same usable space.

Standard or Fully Custom

You can begin from a standard configuration and adjust the room count, bathroom and kitchen layout and finish level, or specify a fully custom plan. The structure is engineered to your load and wind zone in either case, and priced to the final specification — so the quote reflects the home you actually receive, with no open-ended site extras.
